                     (1)     Shareholders’ rights

                             The Board is committed to communicating with shareholders, and makes
                             disclosure in due course about the Company’s major developments to
                             shareholders and investors. The general meeting of the Company provides
                             shareholders and the Board with good communication opportunities. Notices on
                             convening shareholders’ general meetings are dispatched to all shareholders at
                             least 15 clear days prior to the meeting.

                             The Company’s shareholders’ general meetings include annual general meetings
                             and extraordinary general meetings, which are held once each year within 6
                             months of the end of the previous accounting year, and extraordinary general
                             meetings, which are convened in compliance with the Articles of Association and
                             whenever the Board considers appropriate. Shareholders individually or jointly
                             holding a total of more than 10% (inclusive) of the Company’s outstanding shares
                             carrying voting rights on the date of submitting a request are entitled to, by
                             sending the Board or the company secretary a written requisition, ask the Board
                             at any time to convene an extraordinary general meeting to deal with matters
                             specified in the requisition. And such meeting shall be held within two months
                             after the requisition is presented.

                             Shareholders who wish to put forward suggestions during the shareholders’
                             general meeting may raise their hands and speak in order of registration at any
                             time after the resolutions to be considered at the meeting are announced. The
                             Directors and senior management shall respond to the questions and suggestions
                             from shareholders.

                             The Chairman of the Board and the Chairperson of all committees under the
                             Board (or, in whose absence, other members of the committees) will answer any
                             question(s) at the annual general meetings. Pursuant to the Listing Rules, any
                             vote of shareholders at a shareholders’ general meeting must be taken by poll.
                             Poll results are deemed resolutions of the meeting.

                             The Board encourages shareholders to attend annual general meetings to
                             communicate directly about any concern(s) they may have with the Board or
                             the management. Shareholders separately or jointly holding 1% or more of
                             the Company’s shares have the right to put up ad hoc proposals in writing to
                             the Company, and the Company shall include such ad hoc proposals into the
                             agenda for such shareholders’ general meeting if they are matters falling within
                             the functions and powers of general meeting. The ad hoc proposals raised by
                             shareholders shall satisfy the following requirements: (i) free of conflicts with
                             the provisions of laws and regulations, and fall into the business scope of the
                             Company and the terms of reference of the general meeting; (ii) with definite
                             topics to discuss and specific matters to resolve; and (iii) submitted or served
                             to the Board in writing ten days prior to the date of the shareholders’ general
                             meeting.

     1.0 ABOUT THE REPORT
             Since 2017, China Datang Corporation Renewable Power Co., Limited. has consistently
             produced Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) Reports. This ESG Report, the ninth
             published by DRP, seeks to update stakeholders on the latest developments and management
             philosophies in ESG work. We recommend reading alongside the “Corporate Governance
             Report” in the annual report for a complete overview of corporate governance.


             Coverage Period

             The ESG Report covers the period from January 1, 2025, to December 31, 2025 (“the
             Reporting Period”), encompassing the Group’s headquarters, branches, and subsidiaries,
             unless otherwise noted. During the Reporting Period, the Group improved its ESG data
             collection work. Environmental KPIs included span 19 branches including their subsidiaries,
             maintaining consistency with the previous coverage period.


             Reference Standards

            The ESG Report is prepared in accordance with Appendix C2 Environmental, Social and
            Governance Reporting Code (“the Code”) of the Rules Governing the Listing of Securities
            on The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong Limited issued by the Hong Kong Stock Exchange
            (“SEHK”). In the preparation process, the principles of Materiality, Quantitative, Balance, and
            Consistency outlined in the Guide have been followed, with reference to relevant standards
            or principles such as the Guiding Opinions on Central Enterprises High Standards for Fulfilling
            Social Responsibilities in the New Era issued by the State-owned Assets Supervision and
            Administration Commission of the State Council (“the SASAC”) and the”Reference Indicator
            System for ESG Special Report of Central Enterprises-Controlled Listed Companies ” issued
            by the SASAC. Upon review and approval by the Group Board of Directors, the ESG Report is
            available in both Chinese and English. In instances of discrepancy, the Chinese version will
            prevail.

             Materiality: Through a materiality assessment process, the Group gauges the impacts of ESG
             topics on internal and external stakeholders, the Board of Directors decides on ESG topics,
             and the management guides and scrutinizes the identification and prioritization of topics by
             materiality;

             Quantitative: Standards, methodologies, assumptions, and calculation tools used, and source
             of conversion factors used, for the reporting of emission/energy consumption are disclosed;
             KPIs in respect of historical date are measurable, and the performance of ESG policies and
             management systems can be evaluated and validated;




94   China Datang Corporation Renewable Power Co., Limited
Environmental, Social and Governance Report (Continued)


Balance: In addition to positive performance, the Report also discloses some negative
indicators, and avoid selections, omissions, or presentation formats that may inappropriately
influence a decisions or judgment by the report reader;

Consistency: Any changes to the methods or KPIs used, or any other relevant factors affecting
a meaningful comparison are disclosed.


Glossary

For the purpose of better presentation and readability, China Datang Corporation Renewable
Power Co., Limited is also referred to as “the Company””DRP”and its subsidiaries
collectively referred to as “the Group” or “We”.


Note on Data

Data presented in the ESG Report is sourced from the Company’s official documents,
statistical reports, and compiled, aggregated, and audited environmental, social, and
governance information. Historical data cited is final statistical data. Any financial data
discrepancies with the annual report should default to the latter. Unless indicated otherwise,
all financial figures in the ESG Report are presented in Renminbi (CNY/RMB).

3.5 Materiality Assessment

    The Group extensively gathered stakeholder feedback to fully understand their
    concerns and expectations. By integrating national macro policies, the latest regulatory
    requirements of the SEHK, the Company’s actual conditions, and industry development
    trends, we systematically identified and formulated a list of material issues. We
    conducted a double materiality assessment and analysis of these focused issues from
    two dimensions: “impact materiality” and “financial materiality,” clearly defining the
    core issues, which are prioritized for disclosure and response in the annual ESG report.
    For the year 2025, a total of 17 material issues were identified. Each issue is prominently
    highlighted in the corresponding chapters of the report, clearly demonstrating the
    Company’s core concerns and key areas of response.

              4.1 Standardizing Corporate Governance

                      Guided by Party building, DRP strictly observes compliance baselines and fully integrates
                      Party leadership into corporate governance. By strengthening the building of the Board
                      of Directors, standardizing the operations of the “Three Meetings”, implementing the
                      “Triple Major and One Large” decision-making mechanism, and deepening central
                      state-owned enterprise(SOE) reforms, the Company continuously refines its governance
                      system and enhances governance effectiveness. Through such standardized and
                      efficient governance, the Company safeguards the high-quality development of the listed
                      company.

                      4.1.1 Corporate Governance

                              The Group strictly observes the “compliance management baseline” for
                              listed companies and continuously optimizes its corporate governance system.
                              It actively promotes the standardized operation of the “Three Meetings” at
                              both the Company and grassroots enterprise levels, implements the “Triple
                              Major and One Large” decision-making system, and enhances corporate
                              governance effectiveness. The Group has strengthened the building of the Board
                              of Directors, revised the”Articles of Association” and the “Rules of Procedure
                              for Shareholders’ Meetings”, and smoothly completed the reform to abolish
                              the Board of Supervisors, thereby comprehensively optimizing and streamlining
                              the corporate governance structure. Furthermore, the Group has formulated and
                              implemented the Board Diversity Policy of the SEHK. Through board elections,
                              it has brought in senior professionals from fields such as finance, accounting,
                              and renewable energy to promote the diverse organizational development of
                              the Board. Fully respecting the opinions and suggestions of the Board, and
                              integrating market capitalization management with project decision-making, the
                              Group organizes external directors to conduct targeted field research, thereby
                              strengthening the performance of directors’ duties and their professional roles,
                              and ensuring scientific and compliant decision-making for the listed company.

              4.2 Operation in Compliance with Laws and Regulations
                      DRP adheres to law-based corporate governance and compliant operations, strictly
                      abiding by national laws and regulations as well as listing rules, and continuously
                      improving the modern enterprise system with Chinese characteristics. By deepening the
                      construction of the rule of law and compliance system, building a strong defense line
                      for integrity in professional conduct, and improving the quality of information disclosure,
                      the Company ensures standardized, transparent, and efficient operations of the listed
                      company, effectively transforming compliance advantages into corporate governance
                      efficacy.

                      4.2.1 Rule of Law and Compliance

                              The Group always strictly abides by the “Company Law of the People’s Republic
                              of China ”, the “Securities Law of the People’s Republic of China ”, the
                              “Code of Corporate Governance for Listed Companies in China ”, the “Code of
                              Corporate Governance ”, and other relevant laws, regulations, and listing rules.
                              It remains committed to perfecting the construction of the internal management
                              system to guarantee the standardized and efficient operation of the listed
                              company.

                              To deepen the construction of the compliance management system and further
                              advance the building of a world-class legal and risk control system, the Group has
                              formulated systems such as the “Measures for the Compliance Management of
                              China Datang Corporation Renewable Power Co., Limited.” and the “Measures
                              for the Management of Legal Review of Important Decisions of China Datang
                              Corporation Renewable Power Co., Limited.” The Group carried out learning
                              activities regarding General Secretary Xi Jinping’s important instructions and
                              spirit, as well as important laws and regulations such as the “Company Law
                              of the People’s Republic of China ”. Focusing on the requirements of the
                              “Implementation Plan for Building a World-Class Rule of Law Enterprise”, the
                              Rule of Law Construction Leading Group (Compliance Management Committee)
                              formulated and issued the “Key Points for Legal and Compliance Work in 2025”,
                              providing guidance for compliance management throughout the year.

                              To strengthen compliance assurance and safeguard high-quality development
                              through the rule of law, the Group adopted multiple measures to enhance
                              compliance management levels. It consolidated compliance awareness by
                              conducting pre-appointment compliance talks for leading cadres. It issued relevant
                              legal risk alert letters to enhance the foresight of prevention and control. It
                              improved the quality and efficiency of compliance management, deepened legal
                              compliance reviews, and maintained a zero record of administrative penalties.
                              Furthermore, the Group strengthened the construction of the legal team,
                              established a legal research mechanism for key and difficult issues, improved
                              professional performance capabilities, and built a tough legal and risk control team.
                              It carried out in-depth normalized thematic activities for publicizing the rule of law,
                              organized a series of training sessions on the rule of law and compliance, and held
                              special lectures on internal control compliance policies and legal interpretations,
                              cultivating a strong atmosphere of lawful and compliant operations.

   5.1.2 Cultivating Emerging Business Models

       We attach great importance to the cultivation and development of new quality
       productive forces, continuously exploring new models of diversified integration
       under the “New Energy+” concept. This drives the transformation of the
       new energy industry from a single-source power supply to a comprehensive
       energy system, building a new paradigm of green development characterized by
       multi-energy complementarity and industrial synergy. In 2025, we accelerated
       the exploration of application models for emerging business formats such as
       “source-grid-load-storage” integration, “hydrogen-ammonia-methanol,” and
       zero-carbon industrial parks, achieving a series of positive results:

       •       The 1,500 MW wind power source-grid-load-storage integration project in
               Ningxia commenced construction. By integrating the entire value chain of
               wind power development, grid supporting facilities, load consumption, and
               energy storage regulation, it aims to build a demonstration benchmark for
               source-grid-load-storage integration in Northwest China.

       •       The Duolun 150 MW wind-solar-storage-hydrogen integration demonstration
               project–the first green hydrogen coupled with coal chemical industry
               demonstration project in China (on the new energy side)–fully entered
               commercial operation.

       •       We focused on tackling key projects such as the offshore wind-to-hydrogen
               zero-carbon industrial park in Fujian and the source-grid-load-storage
               integration project in the Jinqiang zero-carbon mining area in Tacheng,
               Xinjiang. Tailoring measures to local conditions, we constructed zero-carbon
               energy systems featuring “wind/solar + storage + hydrogen production
               + industrial consumption,” advancing zero-carbon industrial park projects
               from planning and design to concrete implementation.

       •       Invested “New Energy + Data Center” direct green power supply project:
               The 500 MW source-grid-load-storage photovoltaic project, which supplies
               green power to the Zhongwei Cloud Base data center, was connected to
               the grid at full capacity.

                                [Case] Chi n a ’ s F i r s t G r e e n H y d r o g e n - C o a l C h e m i c a l P r o j e c t F u l l y
                                         Operational

                                On November 20, the Datang Duolun 150 MW Wind-Solar-Storage-Hydrogen
                                Integration Demonstration Project fully entered commercial operation. This is
                                the first technological demonstration project in China to achieve deep coupling
                                between new energy-based hydrogen production and the coal chemical
                                industry. Located in Duolun County, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, the
                                new energy side of the project was invested in by DRP. It encompasses a 120
                                MW wind farm, a 30 MW photovoltaic power station, and a 22.5 MW/45 MWh
                                energy storage system. Upon reaching full capacity, it will generate 400 million
                                kWh of electricity annually, with 20% of the surplus power fed into the grid. The
                                project utilizes a process where green power generated on the new energy side
                                is transmitted to the hydrogen production facility to produce green hydrogen
                                via water electrolysis. The green hydrogen is then transported to the methanol
                                synthesis inlet of the Datang Duolun Coal Chemical Project to replace grey
                                hydrogen, thereby realizing the integrated application of green hydrogen within
                                coal chemical processes. The project is expected to achieve an annual green
                                hydrogen production of 70.59 million cubic meters and reduce carbon dioxide
                                emissions by 138,800 tons. Its environmental benefit is equivalent to the carbon
                                absorption capacity of 1,400 hectares of mature forest over the course of a
                                year.

   5.1.4 Ensuring Power Supply

       Relying on big data platforms, we strengthen equipment management by
       summarizing common and trend-related issues. We supervise subsidiary
       companies to enhance defect management and ensure timely defect elimination,
       thereby safeguarding profitable power generation. In 2025, power loss due to
       equipment failures decreased by 71% year-on-year, and the completion rate of
       controllable scheduled power generation increased to over 98%.

       •     Promoting the “replacing small with large” repowering of wind
             turbines to improve existing asset efficiency: We screened projects
             suitable for retrofitting, and pushed grassroots enterprises in regions such
             as Inner Mongolia, Gansu, Jilin, Shandong, and Yunnan to finalize project
             feasibility studies while proactively communicating with provincial energy
             authorities. In 2025, projects including Yunnan Luopingshan, Gansu Yumen
             Phase II, Jilin Shuangliao Phases I & II, Jilin Datong, and Gansu Jingtai
             received approval; additionally, 8 projects are currently under application,
             and 30 projects are queued for sequential application.

       •     Tackling key equipment and system issues to reduce unplanned
             outages: We focused on common issues in blades, gearboxes, and pitch
             systems, and collaborated with subsidiary companies to jointly resolve
             them, specifically addressing problems such as gearbox axial displacement,
             insufficient blade strength, and irrational pitch system designs. As a
             result, power loss from equipment failures dropped by 65.25% year-on-
             year. We strengthened grid-related safety management by completing
             the rectification of 14 issues across 8 regions, successfully meeting
             requirements such as primary frequency regulation and High Voltage
             Ride-Through (HVRT). This effectively helped wind farms avoid penalties
             under the “Two Detailed Rules” assessment and prevented “priority
             curtailment.”

6.0 SYMBIOSIS IN A “NEW” REALM, SAFEGUARDING THE
    ECO-ENVIRONMENT
    DRP upholds the concept that “lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets,” deeply
    integrating ecological priority into the entire process of green and low-carbon development. We
    strengthen climate risk governance, strictly observe environmental compliance bottom lines,
    safeguard natural ecosystems, and achieve highly efficient resource utilization. By empowering
    high-quality development through green and low-carbon operations, we are dedicated to
    safeguarding a “New” realm of harmonious coexistence between humanity and nature,
    contributing solid new energy strength to the building of a Beautiful China.


    6.1 Addressing Climate Change

            Facing the global challenge of climate change, the Group deeply recognizes its potential
            impacts on corporate operations, proactively aligns with the national “Dual Carbon”
            strategic goals, and continuously enhances its capacity to respond to climate change.
            During the Reporting Period, based on the four core elements of the TCFD1 framework–
            Governance, Strategy, Risk Management, and Metrics and Targets–we identified and
            mapped the climate-related risks and opportunities that our business operations may
            face. By formulating targeted policies and measures and driving their cross-departmental
            implementation, we aim to propel the green, low-carbon, and high-quality development
            of the enterprise. On the basis of comprehensive identification and analysis, the Group
            has established and improved relevant institutional systems to effectively address the
            challenges brought by climate change and seize the opportunities therein, thereby
            creating greater value for the company.

            6.1.1 Governance

                    As the core decision-making body for ESG governance, the Board of Directors
                    of the Group attaches great importance to climate change-related issues.
                    Recognizing that climate change may pose potential risks to the Group’s
                    operations and development, the Board has authorized the ESG Working Group
                    to comprehensively carry out climate risk identification and assessment. The
                    ESG Working Group is responsible for formulating climate change response
                    and adaptation strategies, defining relevant goals and targets, building a risk
                    management system, and submitting relevant plans to the Board for review and
                    approval. To ensure the effective implementation of various measures, the ESG
                    Working Group regularly tracks the progress of goal execution and dynamically
                    optimizes and adjusts plans in response to changes in the policy environment
                    and international standards. Furthermore, it strengthens cross-departmental
                    collaboration to coordinate the implementation of climate-related policies and
                    goals, and regularly reports work progress to the Board, ensuring that the Group’s
                    efforts to address climate change proceed in a standardized, efficient, and orderly
                    manner.

                      6.2.2 Environmental Risk Management

                              The Group attaches great importance to environmental risk management.
                              By strictly implementing environmental protection policies for engineering
                              construction and the “Three Simultaneous” principle, building a standardized
                              emergency management system for sudden environmental incidents, and
                              strengthening full-lifecycle ecosystem protection, we make coordinated efforts
                              in environmental risk control, emergency plan management, and ecosystem
                              protection. These measures effectively mitigate environmental risks and safeguard
                              ecological security, achieving an organic unity of environmental and economic
                              benefits.

                              6.2.2.1 Environmental Risk Control

                                      The Group’s engineering construction adheres to the policy of “safety
                                      first, prevention foremost” and strictly executes the “Three Simultaneous”
                                      principle, which requires environmental protection facilities to be designed,
                                      constructed, and commissioned simultaneously with the main project. In
                                      terms of management, we implement a system of unified management
                                      with tiered responsibilities, comprehensively fulfilling labor safety and
                                      environmental protection duties. During construction, tailored environmental
                                      protection measures are formulated for specific pollution sources–such
                                      as exhaust gas, wastewater, solid waste, dust, noise, and vibration–to
                                      minimize impacts on the surrounding environment. Simultaneously, we
                                      strictly regulate the clearance and disposal of construction and domestic
                                      waste, implement the separation of clean and polluted drainage, and
                                      strictly control earthwork operations in accordance with construction plans
                                      to prevent soil erosion. During the Reporting Period, all projects achieved
                                      a 100% compliance rate for the ecological and environmental protection
                                      “Three Simultaneous” requirements, successfully eliminating any new
                                      ecological or environmental compliance issues.

                              6.2.2.2 Environmental Emergency Contingency Plans

                                      The Group proactively builds a standardized emergency management
                                      system for sudden environmental incidents. We issued the “Measures for
                                      the Management of Emergency Contingency Plans for Sudden Incidents
                                      of China Datang Corporation Renewable Power Co., Ltd.”, clarifying that
                                      enterprises at all levels are the main entities responsible for the Group’s
                                      emergency plan management. Grassroots enterprises strictly follow the
                                      requirements of emergency plans to implement the emergency command
                                      system, form emergency rescue teams, and conduct emergency training
                                      and practical drills, continuously strengthening employees’ emergency
                                      response and on-site handling capabilities. During the Reporting Period, the
                                      Group experienced no major sudden environmental incidents.

          6.2.2.3 Ecosystem Protection

                The Group actively supervises grassroots units in strengthening source
                governance. We uphold the principle of placing equal emphasis on
                resource development and ecological protection, adhering to the approach
                of “protecting during development, developing during protection, and
                governing simultaneously with development” to comprehensively execute
                ecological protection and restoration work. We meticulously carry out
                ecological protection throughout the entire lifecycle of new energy
                projects–covering construction, operation, and decommissioning–strictly
                implementing protection and restoration requirements at each stage to
                minimize the impact of project development on ecosystems. During the
                Reporting Period, the Group actively promoted vegetation restoration at the
                Phase II Gaoren Photovoltaic Project in Pingluo, Ningxia. Alongside restoring
                vegetation disturbed by construction, we implemented straw checkerboard
                sand barrier treatments in the original desertified areas. This significantly
                improved the local ecological environment and contributed to the ecological
                protection and high-quality development of the Yellow River Basin.

    6.3.1 Strengthening Pollution Prevention and Control

          The Group actively practices the concept that “lucid waters and lush mountains
          are invaluable assets,” and strictly complies with relevant laws and regulations,
          including the “Environmental Protection Law of the People’s Republic of
          China ”, the “Air Pollution Prevention and Control Law of the People’s Republic
          of China ”, and the “Water Pollution Prevention and Control Law of the People’s
          Republic of China ”. Throughout the entire production and operation process,
          we strictly control the generation and emission of various pollutants and adopt
          targeted treatment measures. This ensures that our emission activities comply
          with relevant regulations, minimizing the impact on the ecological environment to
          the greatest extent possible.

                              The Group is committed to providing clean energy to society, with new energy
                              power generation accounting for 100% of our total output. Our primary power
                              generation businesses consist of wind power and photovoltaic power. The power
                              generation and operation stage produces no pollutants such as exhaust gas,
                              wastewater, or dust; therefore, it has no adverse impact on the atmosphere,
                              ecology, and surface and groundwater environments of the project locations.
                              Currently, the waste generated primarily originates from normal operational
                              activities. To address this, we have formulated relevant management systems to
                              reduce pollutant and waste emissions during operations, earnestly fulfilling our
                              primary responsibility for ecological and environmental protection.

                              6.3.1.1 Exhaust Emissions

                                      During the Reporting Period, the Group’s main source of atmospheric
                                      pollutants was exhaust emissions from company vehicles, which contained
                                      pollutants such as nitrogen oxides and sulfur dioxide. The emission
                                      reduction measures we implemented include:

                                      ➢       Reducing the impact on construction sites and surrounding
                                              environments during engineering construction. Based on the potential
                                              pollution and environmental hazards caused by polluted gases,
                                              wastewater, waste residue, dust, radioactive substances, as well as
                                              noise and vibration generated during construction or other activities,
                                              we formulate specific environmental protection measures.

                                      ➢       Phasing out high-energy-consuming equipment and facilities, and
                                              selecting energy-saving machinery and transport vehicles to reduce
                                              exhaust emissions. We strengthen the maintenance and servicing
                                              of vehicles, strictly prohibiting faulty construction machinery and
                                              transport vehicles from operating on roads. For equipment with high
                                              exhaust volumes and pollutant concentrations, we install exhaust
                                              purification devices to reduce the concentration of pollutants in the
                                              exhaust gas.

       6.3.1.3 Wastewater Discharge

             During the Reporting Period, the Group strictly implemented source-based
             classification and management of wastewater, ensuring that production
             and cleaning wastewater is compliantly discharged into dedicated pipelines.
             Highly concentrated residual liquids are stored at designated sites and
             entrusted to qualified agencies for professional disposal to fully safeguard
             environmental security. The emission reduction measures we implemented
             include:

             ➢      During the engineering construction phase, strictly implementing the
                    separation system for clean and polluted water from construction
                    and domestic use, and rationally planning discharge routes;
                    standardizing earthwork excavation, backfilling, stockpiling, and site
                    leveling operations, and strictly controlling them in accordance with
                    construction organization design plans and specified time periods to
                    effectively prevent localized soil erosion.

             ➢      All stations regularly monitoring and maintaining wastewater
                    collection tanks to ensure normal facility operation and compliant
                    capacity; if excessive accumulation of wastewater affects drainage
                    efficiency, immediately contacting professional wastewater treatment
                    agencies for emergency disposal to strictly prevent environmental
                    pollution caused by wastewater overflow.




                                                                            Annual Report 2025   135
      Environmental, Social and Governance Report (Continued)


                                      ➢       Strictly prohibiting the unauthorized flushing of wastewater pipelines;
                                              should such operations be absolutely necessary, prior application
                                              and approval from higher-level management must be obtained, and
                                              necessary environmental protection measures must be implemented
                                              simultaneously to eliminate any adverse impacts on the environment.

                                      ➢       Strengthening the standardized management of domestic waste
                                              by ensuring timely clearance and disposal to prevent pollutants
                                              from leaching into water bodies due to rainwater washing; strictly
                                              prohibiting the pouring of waste, such as residual oil or food scraps,
                                              into wastewater pipelines to ensure pipelines remain unobstructed
                                              and the environment stays sanitary; strictly prohibiting the use of
                                              phosphorus-containing detergents for tableware cleaning to further
                                              reduce water pollution.

                                      ➢       Regularly conducting inspections and assessments of the soil and
                                              water conservation status and the operational status of environmental
                                              protection facilities at each station. Any facility damage or
                                              environmental pollution caused by poor management is handled
                                              strictly in accordance with the work safety reward and punishment
                                              systems of respective subsidiaries, upholding the bottom line of
                                              environmental safety and promoting sustainable development.

    With the promotion of green and low-carbon development as our core focus, DRP firmly
    fosters a strong sense of mission, responsibility, and urgency regarding the green and
    low-carbon transition, striving to be a promoter, pioneer, and leader in the new energy
    industry revolution. The Group strictly complies with relevant laws and regulations,
    including the “Energy Conservation Law of the People’s Republic of China ”, the “Water
    Law of the People’s Republic of China ”, and the “Cleaner Production Promotion Law
    of the People’s Republic of China ”. Anchoring on our development vision to become
    a world-class new energy supplier characterized by being “green and low-carbon
    development, multi-energy integration, efficient synergy, and digital intelligence,” we
    are steadily advancing various green operations.

                      During the Reporting Period, the Group successfully obtained all required operational
                      water supply through municipal water supply network, ensuring a stable and
                      uninterrupted water supply. At the same time, none of the products or services provided
                      by the Group involve the use of packaging materials, thereby reducing resource
                      consumption and environmental impact at the source. Through comprehensive internal
                      analysis, the Group has continuously optimized the efficiency of various resource
                      utilizations in line with current operational realities, strengthened controls over energy
                      efficiency, resolutely eliminated energy waste, and promoted the maximization of
                      resource utilization benefits.

                      The Group attaches great importance to the daily management of its office spaces,
                      actively promoting the application of energy-saving technologies and the upgrading
                      and retrofitting of operational equipment to continuously enhance energy utilization
                      efficiency. Simultaneously, we have formulated specific policies such as the “Energy
                      Conservation Management System” and the “Technical Supervision Standards for
                      Energy Conservation” to urge and guide all employees to practice green concepts and
                      utilize energy and resources rationally in their daily work. To implement the Group’s
                      green development philosophy, we have specifically adopted the following measures:

                      ➢       Deepening green office practices. We advocate reducing the frequency of air
                              conditioning use in offices, setting the summer room temperature no lower than
                              26 degrees Celsius, and strictly prohibiting the operation of air conditioners with
                              doors or windows open. We comprehensively promote energy-efficient lighting
                              and enforce the rule of “turning off lights when leaving.” We reasonably control
                              the temperature in work and rest areas, standardize the use of electric heaters,
                              and have formulated specific energy-saving management measures. Furthermore,
                              we strengthen power management for office equipment by setting computers to
                              automatic sleep mode and implementing post-work shutdown checks, effectively
                              eliminating standby power consumption.

                      ➢       Strengthening water resource risk management. We are committed to reducing
                              water consumption. Leveraging opportunities such as World Environment Day
                              (June 5th) and National Energy Conservation Week, we conduct multi-dimensional
                              water conservation awareness and education campaigns to earnestly enhance all
                              employees’ awareness of water resource protection, ensuring that water-saving
                              actions yield tangible results.

                      ➢       Promoting the circular utilization of resources. We comprehensively implement
                              paperless office operations and double-sided printing, encouraging employees
                              to widely use electronic documents and emails for work communication. This
                              simplifies workflows, improves office efficiency, and effectively reduces resource
                              waste. We also extensively carry out the repair and utilization of old items,
                              professionally restoring and reusing equipment with residual value, achieving
                              a win-win outcome in cost reduction, efficiency enhancement, and energy
                              conservation and emission reduction.

                      ➢       Promoting the ethos of diligence and thrift. We deeply carry out the “Clean Plate
                              Campaign,” popularize the concept of “Civilized Dining Tables,” and resolutely
                              put an end to food waste. We advocate healthy and civilized dining habits, guide
                              employees to practice the virtue of thrift, and work together to build a green
                              dining environment.

   7.3.3 Protecting Occupational Health

       The Group consistently prioritizes employee health, deeply integrating it into the
       building of a “Happiness Datang.” Strictly following the “Law of the People’s
       Republic of China on the Prevention and Control of Occupational Diseases ”,
       we are committed to building a full-employee, full-lifecycle occupational health
       management system. Adhering to the principle of “prevention first, combined
       with treatment,” we rely on the construction of smart wind farms and utilize
       technologies such as 5G+AI intelligent video analysis and real-time dust and noise
       monitoring to implement dynamic risk management and control over operating
       environments like wind farms, accurately identifying and rectifying hazards. We
       strictly execute the full-process management of Personal Protective Equipment
       (PPE), ensuring scientific selection, comprehensive allocation, and standardized
       use to build a solid safety defense line for employees.

        The Group continuously improves its occupational health surveillance system,
        setting differentiated physical examination items based on the risks of different
        positions. We establish dynamic electronic health records for employees and
        provide personalized health guidance to ensure “early detection and early
        intervention” of health issues. We routinely conduct multi-level and multi-
        form training on occupational disease prevention, PPE usage, and first-aid skills,
        comprehensively enhancing employees’ safety protection awareness and
        emergency response capabilities. In 2025, the Group recorded 4,647 participant-
        times in occupational health and safety training, with a 0% incidence rate of
        occupational diseases; the coverage rates for both occupational health physical
        examinations and health records reached 100%.

    In the new landscape of the era, we take green energy as our foundation and quality service

    From safeguarding data security to practicing transparent procurement, and from empowering

    8.1 Providing Quality Services

          Taking high-quality development as the main thread and adhering to the philosophy of
          “safety as the foundation, quality as the soul,” we coordinate and advance responsible
          marketing, information security, and intellectual property protection to achieve the deep
          integration of corporate development and customer value.

          8.1.1 Adhering to Responsible Marketing

                The Group strictly complies with laws and regulations related to advertising, such
                as the “Advertising Law of the People’s Republic of China ” and the “Anti-
                Unfair Competition Law of the People’s Republic of China ”, ensuring the
                reliable quality of new energy power supply and the legality and compliance of
                marketing behaviors. Upholding the principle of honest operation, we eliminate
                false advertising and fully safeguard customers’ right to know through accurate
                and transparent information delivery. In power supply services, we prioritize users’
                electrical safety, provide comprehensive and refined services, and ensure that
                every kilowatt-hour of electricity is safe and reliable. During the reporting period,
                the Company achieved “zero complaints” in new energy power supply.

          8.1.2 Safeguarding Information Security

                We strictly implement internal systems such as the “Measures for the
                Management of Data Security”, implement the primary responsibility of the Chief
                Security Officer for cybersecurity, and deeply integrate the protection of customer
                privacy and trade secrets into the entire business process. By controlling core
                links such as internal networks, communication systems, archives management,

                I n terms of technical p ro te cti o n , we re l y o n th e “In te l l i g e n t Si tu ati o n al
                Awareness Platform” to achieve 24/7 intelligent monitoring and routinely conduct

                              The Group regards intellectual property (IP) protection as a key support for
                              innovative development. Strictly following regulations such as the “Copyright

              8.2 Deepening Supply Chain Management

                      We actively align with the wave of green transition, with responsibility as the bond and
                      mutual benefit as the goal. We embed sustainability standards into the full life-cycle
                      management of suppliers, practice transparent procurement, and work alongside our
                      partners to build a green, transparent, and healthy energy supply chain ecosystem.

                      8.2.1 Strengthening Supplier Management

                              The Group strictly complies with laws and regulations such as the “Tendering and
                              Bidding Law of the People’s Republic of China ”, as well as internal regulations
                              including the “Procurement Management Measures for the Headquarters and
                              Subsidiary Headquarters” and the “Supplier Management Measures”. Adhering
                              to the principles of “openness, fairness, and impartiality” as well as “honesty,
                              centralized oversight, tiered execution, continuous assessment, and the promotion
                              of excellence while eliminating substandard performers,” we continuously deepen
                              the full life-cycle management of suppliers.

                              •       Access Management: Based on actual procurement needs, we conduct
                                      strict reviews across dimensions such as basic qualifications, certification
                                      credentials, market reputation, and service capabilities. We are gradually
                                      incorporating sustainability elements–such as environmental protection,
                                      occupational health, safety, and business ethics–into the evaluation system,
                                      prioritizing the selection of green and low-carbon products to guide the
                                      green transformation of the supply chain.

          •     Regular Supervision and Dynamic Evaluation: Following the principle
                of “user-responsible evaluation,” we regularly conduct comprehensive
                evaluations from dimensions including contract fulfillment, production
                and operations, industrial synergy, and green supply chain practices. We
                apply these results to the front-end of framework procurement, forming an
                incentive mechanism where “procurement shares are allocated based on
                performance.”

          •     Exit Mechanism: For suppliers exhibiting a lack of integrity, quality issues,

                ranging from summoning them for interviews and ordering rectification,
                to pursuing liability for breach of contract, and ultimately removal, thereby
                promoting the healthy and sustainable development of the supply chain.

    8.2.2 Practicing Transparent Procurement

          The Group deeply implements the concept of “transparent procurement.”
          We comprehensively enforce codes of conduct for procurement personnel and
          a transparent procurement commitment system, relying on digital supervision
          platforms to firmly prohibit any form of corruption and improper transactions.
          During the reporting period, we required all cooperating suppliers to sign the
          “Transparent Procurement Agreement”, achieving a 100% coverage rate. We
          organized specialized compliance training and integrity awareness campaigns for
          suppliers, utilizing case-based teaching focused on bidding and tendering laws,
          anti-commercial bribery, and environmental and safety red lines. We thoroughly
          carried out campaigns to rectify irregular procurement practices, strengthening
          internal supervision and digital and intelligent early-warning mechanisms to ensure
          reasonable procurement decisions and fair outcomes.


8.3 Engaging in Public Welfare

    The Group consistently keeps in mind the social responsibilities of a central state-
    owned enterprise (SOE), integrating public welfare into the very fabric of its corporate
    development. We coordinate the advancement of rural revitalization and volunteer public
    welfare initiatives, giving back to society with a green ethos and serving the people’s
    livelihood through concrete actions, thereby highlighting Datang’s underlying tone of
    responsibility and dedication to the people.

      Environmental, Social and Governance Report (Continued)


                      8.3.1 Rural Revitalization

                              Closely aligning with the national rural revitalization strategy, we leverage our main
                              advantages in new energy and synergize efforts across industrial empowerment,
                              livelihood improvement, and employment stimulation. We promote integrated
                              models such as “Photovoltaic + Agriculture” and “Wind/Solar + Ecological
                              Governance,” organically combining project construction with rural development
                              to broaden channels for increasing village collective income and creating jobs for
                              local residents. We have deepened the “Three-Support and Three-Assistance,
                              and Five-Sphere Integrated Plan” assistance system to accurately match
                              assistance needs, focusing on upgrading infrastructure, cultivating distinctive
                              industries, and enhancing livelihood well-being. This drives the transition of our
                              assistance from a “blood transfusion” (short-term aid) model to a “blood
                              generation” (self-sustaining) model. In 2025, the Group’s investment in rural
                              revitalization amounted to 4.70 million RMB.


                                [Case] DRP Ningxia Branch Devotes Itself to Assisting Hongde Village,
                                         Painting a New Picture of Rural Revitalization

                                As an energy central SOE rooted in Ningxia, DRP Ningxia Branch resolutely
                                shoulders the political responsibility of rural revitalization. Since 2021, it has
                                been paired to assist Hongde Village in Hongsipu District, Wuzhong City,
                                cumulatively investing over 5 million RMB in assistance funds and benefiting
                                more than 6,000 person-times. Through its distinctive “Three-Support, Three-
                                Assistance and Five-Sphere Integrated Plan” assistance system, it has written
                                a heartwarming and substantial answer sheet for rural revitalization.

                                ➢       Industrial Assistance: Continuously consolidated industrial assistance,
                                        completing the acceptance inspections of industry-specific projects for
                                        372 households in the village (354 households lifted out of poverty and 18
                                        monitored households), ensuring the precise implementation of assistance
                                        policies.

                                ➢       Employment Assistance: Assisted in establishing a “Gig Station”
                                        (casual labor service hub), collaborating with over 80 enterprises, and
                                        cumulatively posting more than 800 jobs, bridging the “last mile” of
                                        employment services.

                                ➢       Educational Assistance: Continuously deepened the “Dream Building
                                        Three Grants(National Scholarship, National Encouragement Scholarship,
                                        and National Grant),” distributing 100,000 RMB in educational assistance
                                        funds throughout the year, benefiting 160 teachers and students in
                                        Hongde Village and Tongyuan Village, using compassion to support the
                                        educational dreams of rural children.

       ➢     Livelihood Assistance: Focused on the urgent difficulties and anxieties

             major governance improvements.

     conducted, a description of significant stakeholders identified, and the process and

      Investor Relations

      I.      EVENTS RELATING TO INVESTOR RELATIONS IN 2025

              1.      Investors’ Routine Visits

                      During the Year, the Group always gave detailed answers to the queries raised by
                      investors and analysts in compliance with the information disclosure rules. The Company
                      had adequate communications and exchange of ideas with investors and analysts from
                      a number of institutions via meetings, telephone calls, emails and WeChat. As of the
                      end of 2025, it held 84 investor’s conferences, which were attended by a total of 496
                      investors.


              2.      Results Briefings

                      During the Year, the Group actively organized and held conference for the 2024 annual
                      results and online conference for the 2025 interim results, with a cumulative attendance
                      of 112 institutions and 131 investors and analysts. We communicated about industry
                      development, business planning, production and operation, and other aspects.


      II.     OUTLOOK FOR MANAGEMENT OF INVESTOR RELATIONS
              IN 2026
              In 2026, the Group will actively implement the State-owned Assets Supervision and
              Administration Commission’s deployment requirements for improving and strengthening
              the market value management of listed companies controlled by central enterprises, and
              take proactive actions to comprehensively promote investor relations management. We will
              continue to build multi-level communication channels with investors, closely monitor changes
              in shareholder structure, and establish comprehensive communication paths for both domestic
              and foreign investors. We will also ensure the smooth holding of regular performance release
              meetings and promote high-quality meetings. We will actively participate in major securities
              firms’ summits, strategy meetings, and timely conduct roadshows and reverse roadshows. We
              will closely follow important policies in the new energy industry and new trends in the capital
              market. Based on the careful performance of regular announcement release work, we will
              strive to improve the information disclosure standards and continuously strengthen positive and
              proactive communication with the capital market. We will deepen the visibility and recognition
              in the capital market, increase the stock’s activity, and promote the simultaneous growth of
              intrinsic value and market value, forming a virtuous cycle of high-quality development.

198   China Datang Corporation Renewable Power Co., Limited
                                                               Human Resources

I.    PROFILE OF HUMAN RESOURCES
      As of 31 December 2025, the Group had 3,821 employees in total, including 1,155 employees
      aged 30 or below, representing approximately 30.23% of the total; 1,510 employees aged
      between 31 to 40, representing approximately 39.52% of the total; 571 employees aged
      between 41 to 50, representing approximately 14.94% of the total; 585 employees aged 51 or
      above, representing approximately 15.31% of the total.


II.   GENDER DIVERSITY OF STAFF
      As at 31 December 2025, among the 3,821 employees of the Group, there were 3,146
      male employees, representing approximately 82.33% of the total; 675 female employees,
      representing approximately 17.67% of the total.

      The differences in the education level, cultural background, occupational background and job
      requirements of employees are the main factors affecting the gender diversity of employees.
      The Company is primarily engaged in renewable energy-related businesses such as wind
      power, which has historically had a high concentration of male employees. The Company
      recognizes the benefits of employee diversity and will promote employee diversity, particularly
      gender diversity, as far as practicable. In order to promote gender diversity as far as possible,
      and on the premise of providing equal employment opportunities, career development and
      promotion opportunities, the Company will continue to bring in various types of professionals
      of different genders and nationalities according to its development needs, cultivate and create
      a team of talents of appropriate size, high-end leadership, reasonable structure and excellent
      quality, so as to establish and maintain the Company’s talent advantage in the industry in
      which it operates and lay a solid foundation for the realization of the Company’s development
      strategy.


III. STAFF INCENTIVES
      Based on its development needs, the Group clearly defined targets for various posts and
      further established, improved the mechanism of KPI+MBO+360 performance assessment
      system, made clear of its approach of stressing on both motivations and regulations, stimulated
      employees’ enthusiasm and initiatives for work; established a working atmosphere that is
      fair and equitable, free and harmonious, that affirms personal values, encourages innovation,
      and with unimpeded information and knowledge sharing, allowing employees to showcase
      their talents in an open and equal environment, stimulating their sense of competition and
      giving full play to their potentials. The Group fully understand the personal needs and career
      development aspirations of our employees and provide them with a career path that suits their
      characteristics, aiming to accomplish mutual development of the employees and the Company.




                                                                                        Annual Report 2025   199
      Human Resources (Continued)


      IV. STAFF REMUNERATION POLICY
              The Group strictly implements national policies on payroll distribution, performs a basic salary
              system based on the position-points salary and adopts various incentive mechanisms to attract
              and keep talents. The Group establishes a sound assessment and evaluation system for staff,
              carries out the remuneration mechanism where the total amount of staff’s salary is linked
              with the result of performance assessment. The Group has made reasonable internal payroll
              distribution to truly arouse the enthusiasm of all the staff and exert the security, incentive and
              restriction functions of remuneration.


      V. STAFF TRAINING
              Guided by the concept of “value-based, efficiency-oriented”, the Company actively carried out
              the plan of building a strong enterprise relying on talents and vigorously worked on building
              up three talents teams in management, technical and skilled personnel. It aimed to gradually
              establish and improve the talents cultivation system with its characteristics through “fostering,
              selecting, motivating and utilizing” talents, thus enabling the talents to play important roles in
              the development of the Company.

              In 2025, the Group provided training programmes on business management, professional
              techniques and production skills, with 100% employees attending the trainings. Average
              hours of training per employee by gender for male and female are 77.32 hours/person and
              72.38 hours/person, respectively. Average hours of training per employee by ranking for senior
              management, heads of department, other office staff and general and technical workers are
              121 hours/person, 90 hours/person, 85 hours/person and 80 hours/person, respectively.


      VI. GUARANTEE OF STAFF RIGHTS
              The Group strictly complies with the Labour Law of the PRC and the Labour Contract Law of
              the PRC and makes contributions to social insurance and housing provident fund for employees
              according to these laws, among which the social insurance includes basic pension insurance,
              medical and maternity insurance, occupational injury insurance and unemployment insurance.
              Based on the actual conditions, the Group has established enterprise annuity and supplemental
              medical insurance, prepared labour protection appliances and regularly organized medical
              examination for staff to further safeguard their vital interests.

OPINION
We have audited the consolidated financial statements of China Datang Corporation Renewable
Power Co., Limited (the “Company”) and its subsidiaries (the “Group”) set out on pages 208 to
347, which comprise the consolidated statement of financial position as at 31 December 2025, and
the consolidated statement of profit or loss, the consolidated statement of comprehensive income,
the consolidated statement of changes in equity and the consolidated statement of cash flows for the
year then ended, and notes to the consolidated financial statements, including material accounting
policy information.

In our opinion, the consolidated financial statements give a true and fair view of the consolidated
financial position of the Group as at 31 December 2025, and of its consolidated financial performance
and its consolidated cash flows for the year then ended in accordance with IFRS Accounting
Standards issued by the International Accounting Standards Board (“IASB”) and have been properly
prepared in compliance with the disclosure requirements of the Hong Kong Companies Ordinance.


BASIS FOR OPINION
We conducted our audit in accordance with International Standards on Auditing (“ISAs”) issued
by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. Our responsibilities under those
standards are further described in the Auditor’s responsibilities for the audit of the consolidated
financial statements section of our report. We are independent of the Group in accordance with the
Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants’ Code of Ethics for Professional Accountants
(the “Code”), as applicable to audits of financial statements of public interest entities. We also have
fulfilled our other ethical responsibilities in accordance with the Code. We believe that the audit
evidence we have obtained is sufficient and appropriate to provide a basis for our opinion.


KEY AUDIT MATTERS
Key audit matters are those matters that, in our professional judgement, were of most significance
in our audit of the consolidated financial statements of the current period. These matters were
addressed in the context of our audit of the consolidated financial statements as a whole, and in
forming our opinion thereon, and we do not provide a separate opinion on these matters. For each
matter below, our description of how our audit addressed the matter is provided in that context.

OTHER INFORMATION INCLUDED IN THE ANNUAL REPORT
The directors of the Company are responsible for the other information. The other information
comprises the information included in the Annual Report, but does not include the consolidated
financial statements and our auditor’s report thereon.

Our opinion on the consolidated financial statements does not cover the other information and we do
not express any form of assurance conclusion thereon.

In connection with our audit of the consolidated financial statements, our responsibility is to read the
other information and, in doing so, consider whether the other information is materially inconsistent
with the consolidated financial statements or our knowledge obtained in the audit or otherwise
appears to be materially misstated. If, based on the work we have performed, we conclude that there
is a material misstatement of this other information, we are required to report that fact. We have
nothing to report in this regard.


RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE DIRECTORS FOR THE CONSOLIDATED
FINANCIAL STATEMENTS
The directors of the Company are responsible for the preparation of the consolidated financial
statements that give a true and fair view in accordance with IFRS Accounting Standards issued by
the IASB and the disclosure requirements of the Hong Kong Companies Ordinance, and for such
internal control as the directors determine is necessary to enable the preparation of consolidated
financial statements that are free from material misstatement, whether due to fraud or error.

In preparing the consolidated financial statements, the directors of the Company are responsible
for assessing the Group’s ability to continue as a going concern, disclosing, as applicable, matters
related to going concern and using the going concern basis of accounting unless the directors of the
Company either intend to liquidate the Group or to cease operations or have no realistic alternative
but to do so.

The directors of the Company are assisted by the Audit Committee in discharging their
responsibilities for overseeing the Group’s financial reporting process.

      AUDITOR’S RESPONSIBILITIES FOR THE AUDIT OF THE
      CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS
      Our objectives are to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the consolidated financial
      statements as a whole are free from material misstatement, whether due to fraud or error, and to
      issue an auditor’s report that includes our opinion. Our report is made solely to you, as a body, and
      for no other purpose. We do not assume responsibility towards or accept liability to any other person
      for the contents of this report.

      Reasonable assurance is a high level of assurance, but is not a guarantee that an audit conducted in
      accordance with ISAs will always detect a material misstatement when it exists. Misstatements can
      arise from fraud or error and are considered material if, individually or in the aggregate, they could
      reasonably be expected to influence the economic decisions of users taken on the basis of these
      consolidated financial statements.

      As part of an audit in accordance with ISAs, we exercise professional judgement and maintain
      professional skepticism throughout the audit. We also:

      •       Identify and assess the risks of material misstatement of the consolidated financial
              statements, whether due to fraud or error, design and perform audit procedures responsive to
              those risks, and obtain audit evidence that is sufficient and appropriate to provide a basis for
              our opinion. The risk of not detecting a material misstatement resulting from fraud is higher
              than for one resulting from error, as fraud may involve collusion, forgery, intentional omissions,
              misrepresentations, or the override of internal control.

      •       Obtain an understanding of internal control relevant to the audit in order to design audit
              procedures that are appropriate in the circumstances, but not for the purpose of expressing an
              opinion on the effectiveness of the Group’s internal control.

      •       Evaluate the appropriateness of accounting policies used and the reasonableness of accounting
              estimates and related disclosures made by the directors.

      •       Conclude on the appropriateness of the directors’ use of the going concern basis of
              accounting and, based on the audit evidence obtained, whether a material uncertainty exists
              related to events or conditions that may cast significant doubt on the Group’s ability to
              continue as a going concern. If we conclude that a material uncertainty exists, we are required
              to draw attention in our auditor’s report to the related disclosures in the consolidated financial
              statements or, if such disclosures are inadequate, to modify our opinion. Our conclusions are
              based on the audit evidence obtained up to the date of our auditor’s report. However, future
              events or conditions may cause the Group to cease to continue as a going concern.

      •       Evaluate the overall presentation, structure and content of the consolidated financial
              statements, including the disclosures, and whether the consolidated financial statements
              represent the underlying transactions and events in a manner that achieves fair presentation.

1.   CORPORATE INFORMATION
     China Datang Corporation Renewable Power Co., Limited (中國大唐集團新能源股份有限公司)
     (the “Company”) was established as a joint stock company with limited liability in the People’s
     Republic of China (the “PRC”) on 9 July 2010, as part of the reorganisation of the wind power
     generation business of China Datang Group Corporation Limited (中 國 大 唐 集 團 有 限 公 司)
     (“Datang Corporation”), a limited liability company established in the PRC and controlled by the
     PRC government. As at 31 December 2025, in the opinion of the directors of the Company, the
     ultimate holding company of the Company was Datang Corporation.

     The Company and its subsidiaries (together, the “Group”) are principally engaged in
     the development, investment, construction and management of wind power and other
     renewable energy sources; research and development, application and promotion of low
     carbon technology; development, sale, testing and maintenance of renewable energy-
     related equipment; power generation; engineering, construction and installation, repair and
     maintenance of domestic and overseas power projects; import and export of renewable
     energy equipment and technologies; foreign investment; as well as renewable energy-related
     consulting services, etc.

     The address of the Company’s registered office is Room 6197, 6/F, Building 4, Courtyard 49,
     Badachu Road of Shijingshan District, Beijing, the PRC.

     The Company’s H shares were listed on The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong Limited (the “Hong
     Kong Stock Exchange”) in December 2010.

           The consolidated financial statements have been prepared in accordance with IFRS
           Accounting Standards (which include all International Financial Reporting Standards,
           International Accounting Standards and Interpretations) issued by the International
           Accounting Standards Board (the “IASB”) and the applicable disclosure requirements of
           the Rules Governing the Listing of Securities on the Hong Kong Companies Ordinance

           designated at fair value through other comprehensive income and financial assets at fair
           value through profit or loss which have been measured at fair value.
